bindings.label: A 35-year-old woman presented 11 weeks postpartum with right breast erythema and pain
Patient had three prior episodes of similar symptoms treated at outside hospitals, with the most recent occurring at 9 weeks postpartum

Medical history includes depression, previous treatment with cabergoline until 2016, normal first-trimester hormone levels, continued excessive milk expression despite weaning attempts, no recurrent headaches or visual changes, menstrual cycle not resumed, and current use of multivitamins
Physical examination revealed a 5 cm × 8 cm area of erythema and induration on the medial aspect of the right breast, no fluctuance, and easily expressed milky nonpurulent discharge from both breasts
Laboratory tests show leukocytosis and elevated CRP
Breast ultrasound shows no abscess or focal lesion
Lactational mastitis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae
Milk culture isolate of Streptococcus agalactiae is susceptible to penicillin
Peripheral blood flow cytometry identified a clonal T-cell population comprising 18% of lymphocytes
